newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Nov 5.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
- Pakistan's president dismissed the government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, charging her for corruption.
- U.S. investigators have yet to find a cause for the explosion of Trans World Airlines Flight 800, even after recovering almost all of the aeroplane's remains from the ocean floor.
- The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has enacted new regulations allowing medical researchers to enroll some patients in studies without their consent.
- A U.S. administration official said Indonesian billionaire James Riady discussed Asian trade policy with President Bill Clinton and his aides during his visits to the White House.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton and his rival Bob Dole of the Republican Party ended their campaigning a day before election day.
- People in Saudi Arabia's religious heartland resent the power wielded by the rulers in the country's capital city.
